source_xy_policy: Keep the bounded x and y axes at extent 3, the empty/X/O cell values, X-first alternating turns, and the rule that a placement requires an empty cell. Do not add gravity or change restart and quit behavior.
neighborhood: Straight lines use bounded steps along x, y, and z, including face and space diagonals. The 3×3×3 cube has 49 winning lines of three cells: 27 axis-aligned lines, 18 face diagonals, and 4 space diagonals. Lines do not wrap.
movement: On a turn, the current player places their mark at any empty (x,y,z) cell. An occupied cell or a placement after a terminal outcome is rejected without changing state. A legal nonterminal placement passes the turn to the other player.
outcomes: A player wins when their placement completes any straight line of three cells in the cube. Check for a win before a draw. If all 27 cells are occupied and no winning line exists, the result is a draw.
presentation: Show the board as the engine-owned continuous cube volume, with X and O at their 3D cell positions. Retain turn, win, and draw status information; do not split the cube into layer panels.
input: Clicking a cell supplies its full (x,y,z) coordinate. The engine-provided '[' and ']' keys and on-screen buttons select a depth layer for picking inner cells. Retain the source restart and quit inputs.
z_equals_one_tests: With z at extent 1, the board has the same nine cells and eight winning lines as the Source 3×3 board.
With z at extent 1, legal placements, alternating turns, wins, draws, and rejected placements must match the Source.

z_gt_one_tests.name: Diagonal within a depth layer wins
Any empty depth cell is playable without support
